Jordan: Heads-up: spotted an edge case in staging — setting safemode.config.ttl_ms to 0 causes a mass config refetch spike across hosts. p95 latency jumped ~3x for the config service. Can we pause the console rollout?
Alisha: Can you repro and drop the minimal logs? which service/client is hammering the endpoint?
Jordan: Repro steps in staging: 1) change safemode.config.ttl_ms -> 0 via console preview 2) publish -> clients invalidate cache immediately. Logs: ```2025-11-03T14:12:03Z config-service INFO: publish change safemode.config.ttl_ms=0 by alisha-console-user
2025-11-03T14:12:03Z client-proxy WARN: cache miss safemode for host=svc-frontend-123
2025-11-03T14:12:04Z config-service WARN: incoming fetches spike qps=3500 baseline=1200 p95=320ms```
devops-bot: :rotating_light: Config change recorded: https://console.redwood.internal/configs/safemode (change-id: c-9f3b). Auto-alert: config-fetch-rate > threshold.
Mike: If TTL=0 is treated as immediate expiry that's expected behavior but we probably shouldn't allow 0 in prod. Two quick options: (A) console validation reject TTL < 1000ms with a blocking modal, (B) runtime interprets 0 as "sticky" (infinite) to avoid thundering herd.
Tara: Backcompat note — some services used TTL=0 intentionally as a signal to always re-evaluate for safety-critical toggles. We can't silently change semantics without contacting owners.
Alisha: Agreed. How about a safer rollout: (1) prevent publish to production via console (block rule), (2) add a dry-run mode where control-plane calculates estimated refetch QPS based on active hosts and TTL delta, (3) temporarily ramp telemetry sampling to 100% for config_fetch events for the first 10 minutes post-change.
Jordan: For the preflight calc we need metrics: active_host_count, current_ttl, new_ttl, avg_fetch_interval, and config_fetch_success_rate. If we simulate: hosts~1200, baseline fetch ~0.1/s/host => baseline qps=120. If TTL->0 we could go to ~1200 qps immediately (worst-case) — that matches the spike.
Mike: That worst-case is the thundering herd. Also clients currently have no jitter and immediate refetch on invalidation. We should push a client debounce: when cache invalidated, clients wait randomized 0-3s jitter before fetching and use exponential backoff on errors. That'll shave peak by ~factor 2-4.
Tara: We also need server-side mitigations: rate-limit config fetch per-client-ip and introduce a short grace window where server returns "stale-ok" header for 2s to let clients stagger. Could break correctness for some users but reduces outages.
Alisha: Telemetry gating: increase sample_rate for config_fetch to 1.0 for 10 minutes and emit a change-event tagged with change-id so we can correlate latency/errors to the change. Add a dashboard panel: change-id, change-author, fetch-qps, p95 latency, 5xx rate, hosts-affected.
devops-bot: Current active hosts: 1,210 (from discovery), baseline fetch qps approx 121. Simulated immediate refetch qps=~1,210 => estimated extra load ~1,089 qps.
Jordan: Proposed immediate actions: (A) pause the specific change c-9f3b, (B) push console guard that blocks TTL<1000ms for prod (opt-out via approval ticket), (C) hotfix runtime to treat TTL<1000ms as 1000ms for 30m to give us breathing room, (D) schedule a proper RFC to discuss semantics of TTL=0.
Mike: I can ship the runtime hotfix (small config-service wrapper) and a console validation bump within the hour, then roll back if owners object. Need +1 from platform and SRE.
Tara: I'll DM owners of the safety-toggles list and open an approval ticket. Also will add a tiny telemetry panel to the config-service dashboard (p95, qps) so oncall can see trends.
Alisha: I'll implement the preflight estimator endpoint in the preview API (inputs: change-id, current_ttl, new_ttl, scope) and output estimated refetch qps and recommended mitigations.
Jordan: Sounds good. Can we add an ops checklist in the change flow: run preflight, increase telemetry sampling, confirm owners tagged, then publish?
Mike: +1. Go for hotfix now? :thumbsup:
Tara: :thumbsup: doing owners notify.
Alisha: I'll start the preview-api PR and mock the estimator with current discovery numbers.
Jordan: Action items summary (I'll paste in the ticket): 1) pause change c-9f3b (done) 2) runtime hotfix to min-ttl=1000ms (Mike) 3) console guard/block TTL<1000ms for prod (Mike) 4) preview preflight estimator API (Alisha) 5) telemetry sampling bump + dashboard (Tara) 6) RFC on TTL=0 semantics and migration plan (Jordan). We'll reconvene in #eng-platform in 45m for status. Thanks.
